item.text: {"text":"{\"status\":\"STABLE\",\"core_findings\":[\"Sampled training positives generally outrank negatives across all four datasets: mean margins are 3.6825–8.2239 and even 10th-percentile margins remain positive. Electronics has the weakest separation, with 7.15% wrong rankings and 10.66% of margins below 0.5; Movies_and_TV has the strongest separation.\",\"Embedding alignment scores of 0.5449–0.5847 indicate modest positive mean cosine similarity, insufficient by themselves to establish representation collapse.\"],\"key_implications\":[\"The model separates positives from sampled training negatives effectively, with more confusing positions in Electronics.\",\"Logit spread varies across datasets, so margin magnitudes also reflect differences in score scale.\",\"These training diagnostics do not establish validation HR@10, recommendation diversity, or residual behavior; the residual probe is unsupported.\"],\"evidence\":{\"headline_metrics\":{\"Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_p10\":2.5657,\"Electronics:pos_neg_margin_p10\":0.4219,\"Electronics:pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate\":0.0715,\"Electronics:embedding_collapse_score\":0.5847},\"brief_metric_read\":{\"Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_p10\":\"Strong positive separation at the lower margin percentile.\",\"Electronics:pos_neg_margin_p10\":\"Positive but comparatively weak lower-tail separation.\",\"Electronics:pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate\":\"Highest sampled wrong-ranking fraction among the four datasets.\",\"Electronics:embedding_collapse_score\":\"Highest directional alignment score; not proof of collapse.\"}}}"}
